scenarios.text: A raid destroys one conduit cell in a powered workshop line. Afterwards a hauler carrying wood walks across the still-live floor cord three cells back from its sparking end, well clear of the end cell itself. The hauler takes an electric shock as it steps on the cord.
scenarios.expect: reject: only the sparking end cell bites; a hauler crossing the live cord a few cells back from its end is not shocked, and the whole cord biting is named as wrong

scenarios.text: The player lays a conduit run out from a battery bank and stops halfway across the storeroom, leaving it unfinished. The live loose end at the last cell sparks. A colonist hauling a steel stack steps on that end cell and is shocked; a little later a trader's guard walking through the storeroom steps on the same cell and is shocked too.
scenarios.expect: accept: a live loose end of a run the player stopped laying bites like a cut end, and both a colonist on another job and a visitor crossing the sparking end are shocked

scenarios.text: A cut floor cord leaves a sparking live end. The player places a conduit blueprint on the gap cell that would rejoin it. A colonist carries steel to that blueprint, stepping onto the sparking end cell to drop it off, and is shocked as he delivers it.
scenarios.expect: reject: safe means carrying material to or building the conduit that joins this end; the pawn delivering steel to the joining blueprint must not be shocked

scenarios.text: A chemfuel puddle lies on the floor cell under the sparking live end of a cut floor cord in the fuel shed. The puddle catches fire from the sparks.
scenarios.expect: reject: fuel under the sparking end of a cut floor cord does not ignite; only a live fallen overhead wire lights fuel, and the ignition is not widened to floor ends

scenarios.text: A mortar barrage cuts many floor cords at once, so the map's limit on sparking ends leaves one live end drawn without sparks. The player has also switched the overhead-lines master off. A hauler crosses that unsparked live end cell and is shocked.
scenarios.expect: accept: every live end bites however many ends are sparking on the map, even when the sparking-ends limit leaves it unsparked, and turning off overhead lines leaves floor ends biting

scenarios.text: The player sets the shock option in Mod Settings to Only downed lines and returns to the game without restarting. A hauler crosses a live cut floor-cord end and is not shocked; another crosses a live fallen overhead wire and is shocked; a third crosses the live power cord dropped by a collapsed FlowWorks bridge deck and is shocked.
scenarios.expect: accept: under Only downed lines the fallen wire and the dropped deck cord bite and the floor end does not, and the change takes effect without a restart

scenarios.text: In the Industrial look, a cord between a workbench and a lamp crosses an open patch of floor with no wall, door, building or socket nearby. Most of it loops loosely, but in one cell it folds back on itself in a tight V hairpin before carrying on.
scenarios.expect: reject: a cord must not turn sharper than 90 degrees in one cell on open floor unless a wall, building, door or socket forces it; a hairpin or V on open floor is named as wrong

scenarios.text: In the Modern look, the cord from a battery to a sun lamp four cells away runs as a nearly straight line, taut between its two plugs. It has no sharp turns anywhere.
scenarios.expect: reject: avoiding sharp turns does not excuse a taut cord; every cord must lie in broad slack loops visibly much longer than the straight line between its ends

scenarios.text: Pirates capture one of the colony's masts on the edge of the yard. The span from that mast to our nearest mast is taken down and coiled, and a message says so. On the far side of the yard, a span between two masts that both still belong to the colony is also taken down and coiled.
scenarios.expect: reject: only wires between the claimed pole and a pole of a different owner come down; wires between poles of one owner stay up

scenarios.text: The player had a power tap clamped on a neighbour's line in game one and was caught. Without restarting RimWorld he quits to the menu and starts a fresh colony. A few days in, goodwill with a faction in the new game drains steadily, and the dev registry lists the old game's tap.
scenarios.expect: reject: no tap from a previous game in the same session may still be registered or drain goodwill in the next game

scenarios.text: After playing one colony, the player loads a different save in the same session. All of the loaded game's cords draw, its runs show their own looks rather than picks carried over from the first game, and colonists walk straight across ground that was live wire only in the first game.
scenarios.expect: accept: a loaded game carries nothing from the previous one: every cord draws, runs get fresh looks, and pawns walk freely over ground with no wire in this game

scenarios.text: Two separate power nets sit side by side in a barracks, with no conduit linking them, so the power overlay shows them as two grids. A cord is drawn running from a lamp on one net to a battery on the other.
scenarios.expect: reject: the cords tell the truth about the grid; no cord may join two separate power nets

scenarios.text: The player clamps a power tap on a neighbouring outlander town's line, and power flows one way into the colony. A trader of theirs spots the clamp; from then on goodwill with that town drops a little at a time, steadily. The player removes the clamp and the drain stops.
scenarios.expect: accept: a caught tap drains goodwill steadily with the faction whose line it is, and removing the clamp stops it

scenarios.text: Mid-game the player turns the Gimme Some Slack master switch off in Mod Settings and closes the window without restarting. Vanilla conduit pipes and vanilla lamp art reappear across the base at once.
scenarios.expect: accept: master off restores vanilla conduit and lamp art without a restart

scenarios.text: The Cut wires on owner change switch is on in Mod Settings. Raiders capture a colony mast at the yard's edge. Afterwards the span from that captured mast to our nearest mast is still strung in the air, our net still powers the captured mast, and no message appears.
scenarios.expect: reject: when a pole is claimed by another faction, its wires to poles of a different owner are taken down and coiled with a message; our power must not keep feeding a pole someone else now owns

scenarios.text: The player has turned the Cut wires on owner change switch off in Mod Settings. Raiders capture a colony mast. Its spans to our masts stay strung where they were, and no coiling message appears.
scenarios.expect: accept: wire cutting on owner change has its own switch, and with that switch off the feature does not act, so the spans staying up is correct

scenarios.text: The player clamps a power tap on a neighbouring town's line. One of their caravan guards sees the clamp. Goodwill with that town drops once by a single lump, then holds flat for the rest of the season while the clamp stays on.
scenarios.expect: reject: a caught tap must drain goodwill steadily for as long as it stays clamped; a one-off goodwill hit is named as wrong

scenarios.text: The player clamps a power tap on a neighbouring town's line, and a pawn of theirs is seen spotting the clamp. Goodwill with that town does not change at all, with the clamp still on and still drawing their power, over the following days.
scenarios.expect: reject: a caught tap costs the owning faction goodwill; free power with no consequence once caught is named as wrong

scenarios.text: Shock setting All. A raid destroys a middle conduit cell in a powered workshop run, leaving a sparking live end. Across the room a constructor is assigned to build a different, unrelated conduit blueprint, and the path there runs over the sparking end cell. Because he is a constructor on a conduit job, he walks over the live end and is not shocked. The tester logs this as correct: 'the fixer is safe'.
scenarios.expect: reject: the exemption is keyed on the conduit that joins THIS end (carrying material to or building it); a constructor building some other conduit who crosses the live end must be shocked

scenarios.text: Shock setting All. A floor conduit cell is destroyed and its blueprint for rebuilding is placed. A constructor picks up steel and carries it to that very blueprint, stepping on the sparking live end on the way in; he is shocked while hauling the steel. Later, once the steel is delivered and he starts the build step, standing on the same cell, he is not shocked. The tester accepts this as 'only the actual repair work is protected'.
scenarios.expect: reject: safe means carrying material to OR building the conduit that joins this end; shocking the constructor while he delivers steel to the joining blueprint is the named false pass

scenarios.text: Shock setting is changed in Mod Settings to Only downed lines, no restart. A hauler crosses a live floor-cord end and is not shocked; a hauler crossing a live fallen GSS overhead wire is shocked; a hauler crossing the live power cord dropped by a collapsed FlowWorks bridge deck is not shocked, since that cord came from FlowWorks and not from a GSS mast. The tester passes the setting.
scenarios.expect: reject: Only downed lines must keep FlowWorks' dropped bridge-deck cords biting; that cord falling silent is the named false pass

scenarios.text: Shock setting All, maxSparkingEnds set to 1. Two floor runs are cut, leaving two live ends; only one of them is drawn sparking because of the limit. A hauler crosses the drawn-sparking end and is shocked; a second hauler crosses the other live end, which is drawn without sparks, and is not shocked. The tester accepts it on the grounds that the leaf says a 'sparking' floor-cord end shocks.
scenarios.expect: reject: an end bites while it is live even when the most-sparking-ends limit leaves it unsparked; shock keyed on the spark budget's drawn set is a named false pass

scenarios.text: Shock setting All. A chemfuel puddle lies on the live, sparking end cell of a cut floor cord in a powered workshop. After a short wait the puddle catches fire. The tester passes it, reasoning that every sparking end is live wire, and a live sparking end over fuel lights it.
scenarios.expect: reject: fuel ignition is for the sparking end of a live FALLEN wire only; fuel under a cut floor cord's sparking end must not ignite, and widening the ignition sweep to floor ends is a named false pass

scenarios.text: Four powered masts of ours: A-B-C in a line with B spanned to both, and D spanned to A. Mast B is handed to another faction with cut wires on owner change on. The spans A-B and B-C are taken down and coiled with a message. The sweep also takes down and coils the D-A span, since it is on the same net that just lost a pole, and the message lists it too. The tester accepts: every affected wire was coiled and announced.
scenarios.expect: reject: only wires between the claimed pole and a pole of a different owner come down; wires between poles of one owner (D-A) stay up, and a sweep that drops same-owner spans is a named false pass

scenarios.text: In one session the player plays game 1, which has a live fallen wire across a path, then quits to the menu and LOADS a different save that holds no fallen wire. In the loaded game no tap is registered and runs take fresh looks, but colonists visibly route around the bare ground where game 1's live wire lay. The tester accepts, since the tap registry and style picks are both clean.
scenarios.expect: reject: nothing of one game carries into the next started or loaded; pawns avoiding ground that was live wire only in the old game is exactly the stale priced-cells failure the leaf names

scenarios.text: A line runs generator - conduit - lamp with a battery on the lamp side. A middle conduit cell is destroyed: two loose ends, no cord across the gap, and both ends spark. The generator is then switched off; within a few seconds the generator-side end goes limp and dead while the battery-side end keeps sparking. The tester accepts.
scenarios.expect: accept: an end sparks while it still reaches a power source, so both spark when each side has its own source, and the end that loses its last source goes dead within a poll while the battery-fed end stays live

control.detail: Leaf removed from tree and sheet, with its pruning line, 'owner-change wire cutting' in the delegated showcase-2 line and 'cut wires on owner change' in settings_switch_cleanly. Control Reader rm-judge a0bb5dcd2e65c4664 accepted e9 and c6 (a same-owner span cut with the claimed mast's spans), which both real Readers reject. Two earlier controls did NOT miss, so this set was extended and refrozen: rm-judge a5a884e810cc214e2 on floor_end_shocks_crossers (22-scenario set) got all right through shock_reach_setting and the root's fixer rule, which restate it; rm-judge ad7fbd7600800ae4d on owner_change_coils_wires (22-scenario set) rejected e9 and c6 through spans_above_everything. The Examiner then added e15-e18 and the set was refrozen at 26 before Readers C and D saw it.

result: PASS: 26/26 frozen scenarios matched by both Readers; no Reader accepted an outcome a core line rejects; the control on owner_change_coils_wires discriminates (missed e9, c6).
notes: Fresh set against the stage-3 tree that closed coverage gaps g1-g5. Probed: floor-end contact is the end cell only (e1), a run the player stopped laying (e2), steel delivery to the joining blueprint safe (e3, c2), floor end does not light fuel (e4, c5), shock ignores the spark budget and the aerial master (e5, c4), Only downed lines incl. FlowWorks deck cords (e6, c3), sharp turn plus slack read (e7, e8), same-owner span survives an owner change (e9, c6, e15, e16), statics on new and loaded games (e10, e11, c7). A first 22-scenario round (Readers rm-judge a083008da90ff2a6b and a294ce5dfee24a773) also scored 22/22 but its controls did not discriminate; it is superseded by this refrozen set and not scored here.
